items.d: Strips carbon dioxide ahead of EDI without dosing caustic, where feed alkalinity is high.
Two trains at [duplex train shares offered] each: one runs while the other is sanitized.
Circulates when storage is full, so water never stands in the membranes.
After DI or EDI, where your microbial target needs more margin. Ultraviolet (UV) lowers the viable count; it does not sanitize.
A concentrate recovery RO stage cuts water to drain where sewer charges or supply limits matter.

blocks.intro: Your proposal states each option's effect on drawings, tests and lead time.

items.q: Our draft URS names stainless steel and hot sanitization. Does PP fit?
items.a: Not as written. Natural polypropylene (PP) is rated 0 to 80 °C, and its pressure rating falls as it heats. If you need a hot loop or stainless product contact, PP is the wrong choice. Otherwise, rewrite those rows in your user requirement specification (URS) as outcomes you can test. Where we still differ, our proposal says where and why.

items.q: How is the PP skid sanitized?
items.a: Skid sanitization: [sanitization method for the PP skid]; heat-sanitizable RO and EDI: [heat-sanitizable RO and EDI, yes or no]. After any chemical sanitization, removal of the sanitant is proven before use (WHO TRS 1033). Routine 80 °C at loop pressure, a hot-held loop or steam needs a polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) or stainless loop [whether we quote PVDF].

Single-pass reverse osmosis (RO) with electrodeionization (EDI) suits feed with moderate dissolved solids. Double pass adds margin on conductivity, total organic carbon and silica for high-solids feed.

items.q: How do you handle cold winter feed?
items.a: Rated at 25 °C, reverse osmosis (RO) can lose a third or more of its output at 5 °C. We size at your coldest feed, or add a heat exchanger.

items.q: Our supply is chloraminated. What changes?
items.a: Pretreatment removes chloramine before the membranes. We design for the ammonia it releases together with CO₂ control.

items.q: How do we know it will pass IQ/OQ?
items.a: The factory acceptance test (FAT) proves function before shipping. The site acceptance test (SAT), then installation and operational qualification (IQ/OQ), prove it on your site and feed water. Your quality unit approves the FAT protocol and can witness it once [shop and test bay ready for visits].

items.q: What keeps the water in specification after handover?
items.a: Three things on your side: sanitization on the agreed schedule, daily conductivity and alarm checks, and a kept log. The operating manual sets each one. A service plan adds our visits and calibrations.
